new_statements.rule_in_words: Ubi is treated as a three-level tone language (H, M, L), tentatively; the visible text makes no statement about word stress or a stress-like accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none visible; the author flags the three-tone analysis itself as a hypothesis
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation-form words (examples díidé 'bird', deenya 'saliva', cùwà 'tree' per the snippet summary). Quote assembled from overlapping Google Books snippets of a paywalled Brill chapter, not from an opened page; confidence accordingly medium.
new_statements.identity_note: Alio 2004 describes Ubi of the Guéra (Tunkul/Mongo area, canton Bidiyo), the same variety as ubii1238; no dialect split is reported (the SIL survey found no pronunciation differences across the six Ubi villages).
